item.title: The Macguffin
item.description: A magical locket that makes whoever touches it triumph over a great evil.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An old locket, when someone touches it they begin on a journey to face some evil person or organization. They’ll defeat the villain in some epic showdown and everyone lives happily ever after.

+ Yay! Happily ever after!
- Yeah, of course there’s more

There’s a few catches. First, someone always touches the locket, it’s destiny. That’s not to say that this is uncontainable, but the journeys need to be managed instead of prevented. Which is especially difficult due to catch two, the Foundation meets all the requirements to be a villain. So their top priority is obviously making sure they never get selected as a target. But then comes in catch three, because the obvious containment method is to simply send someone on a scripted adventure. But when you script the adventure, you become the villain. I don’t know if you’ve caught on by now but this article is all about the Foundation trying to contain fate, which is completely illogical. But the thing is, they do it.

Central Narrative: The meat of the story will be told through test logs where the Foundation will experiment with different containment procedures. For instance, what happens if you have someone touch the locket, then you terminate them? (Spoiler alert, the same thing that happens when the protagonist of a book is facing down a firing squad, it doesn’t end well for the firing squad). In the end, they contain it by having an independent task force act as the villains. The task force doesn’t know they’re meant to be villains, they know that they have one objective, “kill anyone who touches the locket”. They also know that they keep failing. Since the task force isn’t directly controlled by the Foundation, the Foundation is safe from becoming the villains.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Two things. One, fate isn’t that common of a system to show up in SCPs. The second one I haven’t mentioned yet, but this is actually a completely non lethal SCP. The person affected by the locket is both incapable of dying and incapable of killing people. That’s not to say it’s not dangerous though. I’m considering adding a discovery log where someone with this locket collapses a corporation that was exploiting people, but at the same time puts millions of people out of work.

Additional Notes: I want to know if you think this is too many ideas in one or if it ties together well.

item.title: Admin is Asleep, Post Antimemes (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard entry

Elevator Pitch: A rumor spreads through D Class personnel of something infiltrating the Foundation to observe the researchers, containment officers, et cetera. Originally overheard on 06/05/2020, research and containment separate and isolate the D Class personnel and wipe their memories, yet strangely, the rumor returns in each separate group of D Class in merely a week.

Central Narrative: Dr. J. Holloway is intrigued regarding the "impossible rumor" D Class has subscribed to, and turns to interviews with the personnel. They discover each individual group of D Class as a different name for the SCP, one group calling it "the Watchman," another being "the Scribe," and so on. Yet within these tight groups, there have been sightings of the illusive creature, describing it as an elongated humanoid with its legs sharpening to a single tip, its torso gaping to the point of being able to watch its lungs breathe, and what appears to be a briefcase in its hand filled with papers and pencils.

+ show block
– hide block

Although skeptical, Holloway sets the notes aside and, after obtaining permission from the lead officer in containment alongside approval from the head of research, Holloway spends the night in one of the D Class groups. Approximately halfway through the night, Holloway awakens to the sound of rustling papers and the scratches of graphite. They arise from their bed and see the creature, whom they dub "Admin," watching and presumably writing about Holloway. Holloway attempts to communicate with the creature, but to no avail, yet it seems curious over the tone of voice Holloway is using.

Further testing reveals the Admin is quite curious and has an overarching desire to learn the unlearnable. It cannot verbally communicate, but it writes quite well and is an avid enjoyer of learning how living things work.

After the incident, Holloway sends in a formal request to get the creature SCP status. While awaiting approval, they hear of sightings of the creature, sitting and watching the personnel as they rest. While Holloway never directly spoke of the creature, they have chatted with them post Admin sighting. Holloway draws the conclusion that merely speaking with someone who has directly seen the creature was enough to spread it, like a virus.

Through collaboration with the Site Director, cognitohazards with antimemetic properties are set around the site to prevent the "spread" of the SCP, along with limiting Site 23 to no other Keter class SCPs in the event of a containment breach and isolating it from the rest of the Foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of D-is-for-disposable personnel bringing forth sight of a very "contagious" SCP is fun to me.

Additional Notes: I mainly need help tightening the plot!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 35 words over. ~Zyn

item.title: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request / Review
item.description: who will protect who has given us a home
item.content:encoded:
When global warming becomes just another K-Class scenario to the world, who will protect who has given us a home to live on?

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Hello, this will be my first SCP idea/greenlight, and I'm hoping this makes as much sense to the general public as it does to me.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (SCP-5284 preferred, not picky on numbers otherwise)

Elevator Pitch
An iceberg floating just 50 knots North of Antarctica is beholden to many phenomena. For one, the glacier itself seems to react to the shortcomings of mankind, almost being frustrated at the existence of the human race. What exactly is below the surface, and who was responsible for this odd mesh of science and nature?

Central Narrative: The main SCP item is the glacier, and SCP-XXXX-2A is found within the glacier. This is an anomalous gas similar to the C-terminus debacle in SCP-3966 (with the "missing" valence electrons of the oxygen inside SCP-XXXX-2A being monkey paws). When inhaled by a human, they slowly but surely turn into a monkey (hereby SCP-XXXX-2B)

SCP-XXXX-3 are a series of thirteen shrines/steles with an unknown cognitohazardous language. While English operates on a series of words conveying concepts, this language does the exact opposite; communicating in conviction, feeling, empathy.

+ show block
– hide block

Over the course of the article, a journal is found from a monkey who was bestowed intelligence by the Avatar of the Earth. Our monkey scientist then grapples with the stupidity of mankind, before realizing that the only way to protect what gave him the ground to stand on, is to pack everything away and create a failsafe, so that Earth may live on.

End of the article implies that the iceberg is melting faster from this point onwards.

Relies on themes of: Intelligence, nature, and whether the nature of humankind is to create or destroy. Cliché, I know.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Trying to lure readers in with the absurdity of "haha what if the return to monkey meme was real", but trying to take it in a darker more serious sense.

Additional Notes: I've had this idea swimming around in my head for months, and it was either this or writing a Pataphysics skip. Heavily inspired by Silent Spring and my own experiences in the outdoors as an Eagle Scout.

If you made it this far, thank you and I hope you have a wonderful day!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: Last Flight Out (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.description: a cheap flight suddenly pops up on the airport monitors
item.content:encoded:
In the chaotic world of cancelled flights and aiport sleepovers, if a cheap flight suddenly pops up on the airport monitors that seems to good to be true, it's because it probably is…

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (Aiming for SCP-5127)

Elevator Pitch

  • Anomalous airplane
  • Appears at airports that are either closed, either for the night or due to bad weather
  • It's destination is always one in high demand at the current aiport
  • Up to 26 passengers can 'transfer' to this flight
  • Plane does not show up on radar, and does not recieve instruction from air traffic control
  • Flight always lasts 2 hours, 47 minutes from take off to landing
  • Will land in some forsaken place, such as in the middle of Siberia, the Sahara, or even in the ocean
  • Aiport it lands at is also anomalous, appearing from the inside to be an exact copy of whatever aiport the plane was supposed to land at
  • Airport will spontaneously generate about 30 minutes before the plane lands
  • Aiport will remain in existince for exactly 75 minutes, before both it and the airplane disappear

Central Narrative: Honestly I don't really understand what this part is supposed to mean, so for the the time being, I will say None. But please feel free to give me advice on what to put here, as well as how to expand and improve this SCP.

item.title: 'Baby-Aid' - Seeking feedback and Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
'They're trying for a baby? Don't work hard when hardly working's this easy! Baby-Aid!'

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Let's make conception convenient! Just put in a drop of that prime stock D-N-A and receive a child in under an hour! Perfect for the busy mommies and hard working daddies! The children even come out with little improvements, a gift from our home to yours!

Central Narrative: The Foundation recovers numerous instances of the same anomalous appliance from the 1950s found within an old storage unit. Thought to be an unsuccessful product that never went into circulation, the Foundation begins testing the devices different settings using Class-D personnel. They produce children on every setting the machine has, finding each to be differently cybernetic but otherwise non anomalous.

+ show block
– hide block

They designate the SCP safe and put it under secure storage at a low security site and debate what to do with the children; while some more paranoid and morally conscious staff members initially recommend euthanasia, the children are healthy despite their implants and found to develop normally. The children are then placed in Foundation care until they can be neutralised if further anomalies develop from them or they can be integrated into the Foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Initially just an anomalous item, the children produced raise the question of what the Foundation does with the innocent in the aftermath of the anomalous. While the more cynical among us would expect the worst, the Foundation has proven to be surprising and the situation proves both their compassion and their pragmatism.

Additional Notes: I like the idea of a small story and otherwise basic SCP being the catalyst for one of the Foundation's more compassionate moments in history. Sometime I feel they're pushed beyond morally grey pragmatists into villainous territory and think they have the capacity to be kind, even if it's tinged with clinical coldness and only just once in a while.

item.title: Wooden Nickels -Idea for Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout + Addenda

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a life-size wax replica of George Washington. Physically all looks normal excluding it's face, which has been disfigured, leaving only a pair of the president's famous wooden teeth visible. Object will actively roam and attempt to locate wood of any form. If the object senses wood within about a 10 meter radius (through unknown means), object will enter a frenzied state and produce a knife from within it's wax body, designated as SCP-XXXX-1. In the state, entity will attempt to dismantle any wooden matter in the area and begin whittling it down into "wooden nickels". SCP-XXXX-1 is unnaturally efficient at carving wood, with object able to manufacture a coin about every 8 seconds. These coins, designated as SCP-XXXX-2, will upon physical human contact transfigure into a real coin. The coins will maintain this form for 78 hours after initial contact. The type of coin seems to be linked to the type of wood used (research ongoing). Researchers have also observed that entity will also instinctively pick at leaves, which upon human contact will briefly transfigure into the shape of paper currency before melting into pulp.

Central Narrative:
A central focus is the implication that this anomalous object was likely artificially created through unknown means for the express purpose of producing counterfeit currency. Researchers speculate though that object is likely an unsuccessful prototype, evident by a number of "flaws" that would make a counterfeit operation difficult to achieve at scale. This leaves it open for the possibility of other similar objects having been made. Article will also detail the acquisition of the object and the discovery of a violent reaction the object has when it becomes conscious that it possesses wood on it's body (the disfigurement of it's face was a result of attempts to remove them).

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I plan to attach a photo of the entity that will hopefully hook the reader into learning more and will draw them in further with the idea that this object was made for a criminal purpose by and unknown creator.

Additional Notes: N/A

item.title: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Are they just zombies? No! Because instead of hands they have really cool things!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

Elevator Pitch: A small town, a dad who's the leader of an amateur thaumaturgical cult, and his 9-year old kid with a notebook titled "Really cool stuff". One fateful day, the young kid sneaks into his dads basement and places his notebook at the center of the ritual setup, unleashing everything within it.

Central Narrative: Follow a team of daring MTF soldiers as they have to fight their way through a city occupied by zombies that all have cool things instead of hands! What do you mean by cool things, you might say? Oh lord, anything! Axes? Yup! Swords? Yup! AK-47s? Of course. Lightsabers, blackpowder cannons, katanas, grenade launchers, nunchucks and chainsaws. If you're lucky you might even run into the zombie with a boombox for hands, that plays only The Final Countdown by Europe, and the volume is set to eleven!

If the brave MTF team make it to the boys house, they have to fight the ultimate enemy. The completely original creation of his called Pikazilla, a 50 ft. tall version of Pikachu that shoots lightning and eats geography teachers.

So greenlight this SCP today and experience the best hard-hitting and uncompromising ACTION of the 80s!

item.title: New Writer Seeking Greenlight: The ANTECHAMBER
item.description: Potential SCP: Several locations around the globe
item.content:encoded:
Potential SCP: Several locations around the globe that let psychics access a metaphysical gateway to Hell; allows them to communicate with the dead

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror (existential, graphic)

Page Layout:
Standard Order: Class; Containment; Description; Discovery; Exploration Logs and Addenda

Elevator Pitch: Several locations around the globe allow psychic individuals to access a metaphysical gateway to Hell. This allows them, and by proxy, the Foundation, to communicate with the dead. This SCP is useful, but dangerous: sometimes, something from the other side hitches a ride back to our world…

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

Certain locations will periodically undergo Virgil Events. During these events, magically skilled or psionically gifted individuals can access a kind of metaphysical lobby, which a mysterious masked attendant. This Antechamber allows access to a vast, spiritual realm full of dead souls and entities, all in perpetual, self-inflicted agony. Mediums can find and speak to deceased individuals, and gain otherwise unobtainable information for the Foundation.

For example, the Foundation uses this SCP to contact a Chaos Insurgent spy who had been killed while trying to sabotage the Foundation; they able to wring out of the confused spirit the name of his accomplice, still hidden in Foundation ranks.

The Foundation sends many Mediums to explore and document the SCP. But over time, this eats away at their sanity. Moreover, there are occasional Geryon Events, where something will follow the Mediums back into the physical realm, and Foundation soldiers have to deal with them.

The SCP is called the Antechamber because the SCP actually refers to the Lobby-like chamber that Mediums experience when they access the SCP, which allows access to all of Hell.

Hook: This article boasts detailed and intense explorations of Hell; it depicts the mental breakdown of those who visit Hell; and it indulges in the occasional badass demon-killing action scene (described via interview logs, as appropriate to an SCP article).

Additional Notes: The ritual that allows access to this SCP was discovered in a book confiscated from a Marshall, Carter, & Dark shipment.

item.title: Final Memory - Greenlight request
item.description: Entity's presence can only be recalled in old/faded memories.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A "species" of entities that stalk humans and constantly delete themselves from short-term memories, thus rendering themselves effectively invisible and intangible. As memories containing the entity naturally (or unnaturally) fade, memory of the entity itself becomes progressively more vivid. Eventually the entity's presence is all a victim can remember of their past.

Central Narrative: Article will focus on the study of the first two specimens captured by the Foundation, along with their respective human "hosts". Both hosts are elderly and suffer from dementia (implied to be caused/worsened by prolonged exposure to the entities). Host 1's dementia has progressed to a late stage and he expires shortly after entering Foundation custody, experiencing immediate brain-death upon seemingly gaining perfect perception of the entity. Host 2 lives in containment for several months and chronicles her increasingly detailed perception of the entity through artistic depictions.
Eventually a method is found for separating the entity from host 2 and containing it, but, having minimal life prospects even if released from foundation custody, she insists on co-habitating with it in order to continue her series of paintings until death.
Post-brain-death MRI scans of both hosts imply that their entire brains have been re-wired to store a single memory of the entity's true form.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I would like to include a "photograph" of one of host 2's paintings to give the entity's some visual flavour. In practice this means stealing a painting from some modern artist a la Ivan Seal, but I've yet to find a painting that is both appropriate and sufficiently obscure.

Additional Notes: I've gradually pivoted toward this SCP being "dementia themed" in a vague sense, as I found a central idea like that helped to keep the article cohesive even if it's not explicitly mentioned. It might also shamelessly capitalize on the current popularity of Everywhere at the End of Time, which would be a nice bonus.

item.title: Unwilling Houdini
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes please

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: the base idea is a humanoid entity that cannot be contained, restricted, or willed to do something in any way shape or form, even if willingly. Without a some form of freak accident causing there “escape” It’s an scp designed by an outside group, as a trap for the foundation. The following is a sample list of attempted form of containment

attempt: result:
Standard police issued handcuffs Handcuffs seemed to be faulty falling off after the slightest movement from the scp
Held down by two armed officers Both suffered from Petit mal seizures simultaneously despite having no history of epilepsy
The tactics used by casinos to make sure the house always wins The scp breaks the banks of multiple Casinos before being accused of fowl play resulting in police trying to arrest him
Subject willing turns himself in and is escorted to local jail cell Door unable to close due to mysterious jam, and when the scp leans against a nearby wall it crumbles backwards causing him to fall out of the cell. Into the alleyway behind it

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: the foundation finds the scp after it unintentionally causes a mass prison break. They take it into custody causing a string of freak accidents and a site-wide containment breach. They soon find that the only way to keep the people safe from the scp is with anti-containment measures. A system of covert actions taken to make sure that the scp is on no way shape or form confined to one area due to another persons actions, this way his anomalous properties are never activated. However this proves far more difficult then they thought

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the main hook is effort needed by the foundation in order to keep the anti-containment measures in place. Because as seen above if the scp gets arrested or walks into the wrong place it can cause all sorts of problems. Meaning that every person staffed on this scp has to be extremely careful wi the there actions. Or they risk the anti-containment failing, the with the fallout scaling with the size and effect of the containment, wether physical or metaphorical.

Additional Notes: this is my first scp in a list designed by an outside force to screw with the foundation, starting small now to test the waters.

item.title: Connection Lost - seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/emotional

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous friendship bracelet kit (possibly from Dr. Wondertainment) that anomalously links those who wear created friendship bracelets. Effects vary depending on what materials are used in the bracelets, letter beads could allow telepathic communication between the wearers etc.

Central Narrative: The central narrative is told through several diary entries and notes left between the two previous owners. The story is about two close friends who drift apart, despite being anomalously linked. Diary entries will be from the perspective of Angela, who is doing everything she can to not lose Bri (her best friend) who moved away. Bri slowly pulls away and starts going down a different path than her friend. Angela knows this, but still fights to keep her best friend. This proved unsuccessful in the end however, as Bri suddenly cut ties with Angela, evidently removing the bracelet and all other methods of communication. About a month after this, Angela receives a letter along with Bri's bracelet and half of the kit.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is primarily a story about two friends who drifted apart despite everything available to keep them together. I believe this is a story that many people can empathize with through personal experience, and thus will probably elicit an emotional response.

Additional Notes: I intend on drawing on my own personal experience when creating this story, and hope that this will allow others to empathize with my characters. I will determine the extraneous effects of the bracelets materials as I write the story, as the SCP is more of a vessel to tell it.

item.title: S.C.P. Idea | Greenlight Request
item.description: Summary of S.C.P.: Volcanoite and Magmaite.
item.content:encoded:
In short, Magmamite and Volcanoite in their "first-form" will be simple rocks; big rocks enough to fit in your hand. Volcanoite is constructed out of volcanic matter such as molten rock, and has a crater in the middle for something-magmamite-to be placed in with a thin frontier around it. Magmamite it a lava-red/orange rock with a gloss-cover with fractures filled with black dried-up igneous rock.

Magmamite's ability is to generate a small, sluggish body of lava and whatever comes in contact with the lava is then infused and gives "it" more lava to use.

Volcanoite's ability is to generate, with the heat, to make a volcano. (Height varies.)

Both of these combined give the power to generate a large, active volcano- and a dangerous threat to the worlds climate change.

I'm new to S.C.P writing, so any help or feedback, or even questions would be great.

+ "Inside" stuff...!
- Go back...

Those who physically see or are within twenty meters will experience some sort of "flashback" or "memory" inducement, depending on which one they are- Volcanic has been described as some sort of man, and Magmamite as some sort of Girl.

item.title: Ms. G. Lass
item.description: Glass lady is smoking hot. Literally.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXX has no bodily orifices and all their skin is replaced with glass. The rest of them is hollow. They were created in a glass factory explosion in Toulouse, France. They were formerly known as Georgine Lass. They were the only survivor. They have a strong hatred for transparent objects due to this, and will attempt to crack, break, or otherwise damage them when in line of sight. When exposed to even a very small amount of oxygen, they will engulf in flames reaching a temperature of 4000K. When this happens, they begin to run around erratically, usually burning though everything and everyone it comes close too.

Central Narrative: Due to the severe flammability, all methods that foundation has thus far have been found not heat resistant enough, hence ineffective. It follows the logs of a pair of containment engineers working, getting pressured, mishaps, everything, as they try to create a containment chamber capable of containing them as they posed a severe containment risk and breached containment several times. They eventually do succeed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be 2 versions of the file, 1 before the success, and 1 after. The before one will have an O5 notice stating “All Containment Engineer Personal at Site X, unless told otherwise by a Foundation Employee with Level 4 Clearance or above, must focus all research, time, and resources to the creation of a containment chamber for SCP-XXX. The budget for containment has been increased to [Large Amount Of Site’s Local Currency].”

Additional Notes: It's not just containment breaches 24/7, but more 1 monthly give or take. I will also have a recontainment procedure so it's not like it takes days to recontain.

item.title: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.description: Hi. After studying the site for a while I've written up my first idea for an SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional and symbolic, with undertones of mystery and light comedic moments

Page Layout: Traditional, with an account of the recovery, and addendum containing testing logs, and a few interviews.

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious black, metal object resembling an hourglass appears in the sky above a foundation site and crashes through the roof. The object appears to consume the time of living beings near it, causing them to leap forward in time and age accordingly. The object ends up killing several researchers, but one seems to be unaffected. The object later even goes as far as to attach itself to him. This researcher then has to grapple with survivor's guilt, and must learn to keep moving forward, accepting both the good and the bad of the object being attached to him.

Central Narrative: (Ultimately, I want to tell a human story about a man initially struggling with guilt, but with the help of a friend, is able to accept the way things are and work to move forward.) After crashing into a foundation site, the SCP lands near a researcher. The anomaly then proceeds to scan him. After the anomaly is contained, the research wants to learn more about it, and is appointed head researcher. During a routine examination, the SCP activates, while our main researcher and two others are in the room. The two other researchers are killed by the SCP, but our main researcher is left. Later, the SCP permanently attaches itself to him. Through interviews with Dr. Glass, we learn he is suffering with survivor’s guilt and isolation. During subsequent testing, we find out that the SCP can allow the researcher to exist outside of time. (Time stop) The end of the arc will have the researcher coming to terms with the conflict he feels towards the SCP being attached to him and using it to help the foundation/the world, while leaving the origin and purpose of the SCP open ended.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: In addition to a relatable human struggle, throughout the article, there’s hints here and there that the SCP may have been intentionally created by an unknown group.

Additional Notes: I’m hoping to expand on the backstory of the SCP in future tales or articles, as well as feature the researcher in some of my future articles. While I couldn’t explain every detail here, I have the main arc of the story pretty well thought out. Critique and greenlights welcome.
